en.title: Egyptian lentil soup

en.title: Koshari
en.intro: Cairo's street food: rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas under spiced tomato sauce and crisp fried onions, with garlic vinegar on the side. The fried onions need an oil thermometer; a device without one refuses that step.

steps.n1: Bring the lentils and water to the boil.
steps.n2: Simmer until tender but whole (20 to 30 minutes).
steps.n4: Bring the salted pasta water to the boil.
steps.n5: Cook the macaroni until al dente, stirring now and then.
steps.n7: Heat the oil in the rice pot.
steps.n8: Toast the vermicelli, stirring constantly, until golden.
steps.n9: Add the rice, hot water and salt; bring to the boil.
steps.n10: Lowest heat, lid on, until the water is absorbed (12 to 16 minutes).
steps.n12: Toss the onions with the flour.
steps.n13: Heat the frying oil to 175 °C, measured with a thermometer. The pot must be no more than half full.
steps.n14: Deep-fry the onions in batches at 175 °C until deep golden brown (5 to 9 minutes a batch). Lift out with the skimmer and drain.
steps.n16: Fry the garlic, cumin, coriander and chili in a spoon of hot oil for under a minute, until fragrant.
steps.n17: Add the passata, vinegar and salt; simmer until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon (12 to 20 minutes).
steps.n18: Make the daqqa: crushed garlic in vinegar and water with a pinch of cumin and salt.
steps.n19: Layer rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas; spoon sauce over; top with crisp onions.
steps.n20: Serve hot with the daqqa and extra sauce on the side.
